diffs.diff: shunt voltage (V): datasheet reading gives 3.125e-7 per count, the part's model has 0.0001953, 0.02
diffs.evidence: TI INA228 datasheet (SBOSA20), 7.6.1.5 VSHUNT register (04h): 'Conversion factor: 312.5 nV/LSB when ADCRANGE = 0; 78.125 nV/LSB when ADCRANGE = 1'. The second reading's 3.125e-7 V is right, and the model agrees with it: part.json's description says '±163.84 mV, 312.5 nV per count'. The model does not simulate VSHUNT (04h) at all. Its sim only covers VBUS (05h, 195.3125 µV/LSB, which matches the datasheet's 'Conversion factor: 195.3125 µV/LSB') and CURRENT (07h, CURRENT_LSB = 20 µA, which comes from SHUNT_CAL, eq. 2-4). The driver does not read shunt voltage either, so no wrong shunt-voltage constant exists anywhere in the model. The gate flags it only because the quantity is missing from the sim, not because a value differs.

diffs.diff: temperature (C): datasheet reading gives 0.0078125 per count, the part's model has 0.0001953, 0.02
diffs.evidence: TI INA228 datasheet, DIETEMP register (06h): 'Conversion factor: 7.8125 m°C/LSB' (Table 8-x: Temperature –40 °C to +125 °C, 7.8125 m°C/LSB). The second reading's 0.0078125 °C is right. The model never claims a temperature scale: part.json, the sim measures and the driver do not model DIETEMP (06h). review/outcome notes say 'VSHUNT/DIETEMP/POWER are not modelled because 24-bit registers at adjacent addresses overlap in the 16-bit register store'. The model's two scales (195.3125 µV bus, 20 µA current) belong to other quantities, which the datasheet confirms. Nothing in the model is wrong; temperature is just not included.
